assessor: RTS governed build assessment — Semantic Claim Refinement v1
rationale: I safely discovers and lexically extracts official documentation but intentionally leaves novel contract wording as REVIEW_REQUIRED. J adds a bounded repository-local refinement layer that maps only exact source sentences onto a controlled semantic alias ontology. It does not call providers, infer hidden architecture, verify behavior, mutate runtime routing, or grant authority. The main reuse is I's exact-anchor/audit contract plus H's bundle validator.

queries: official docs ambiguous extraction exact anchor

assets.notes: Reuse normalized source text, exact-anchor lexical claims, ambiguity hashes, intake fingerprint and H-valid bundle boundary.
Reuse claim schema, supported contract areas and strict bundle validation.
Reuse live-smoke ambiguity baseline and destructive DA lessons.

gaps: No component currently reduces I REVIEW_REQUIRED blocks using a controlled semantic ontology while preserving exact anchors and uncertainty.
No current verifier explicitly prevents negation reversal or multi-rule semantic ambiguity during review reduction.

risks: Semantic aliases can overgeneralize provider wording.
Negated or exception clauses can be mistaken for positive support.
One sentence may legitimately refer to multiple contract areas and should remain reviewable if classification is not unique.
Reducing review count can become a vanity metric if unresolved high-risk text is silently hidden.
Upstream ambiguity truncation can create false completeness.
